summary: Fire tower now built into a water tank on Naval Weapons Station Crane, Martin County, IN; cab gone, no public access; NHLR-registered August 2026.

facts.status_note: Stands inside a water tank, with its cab no longer in place.

access.note: On restricted federal Naval property with no public access (Indiana Fire Towers, February 2025 visit).

events.note: By 1946 a water tower stood built over and around an old Forest Service lookout tower, per a survey-mark station description. No build date for either structure is given.
Caption on the Indiana Fire Towers page says a 1978 topographic map shows a water tank with a lookout tower.
Visited in February 2025 by Indiana Fire Towers, which describes this tower as now part of a water tank tower.
Registered August 2, 2026 as US 1839, IN 19; nominated by Jason Johns.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1946 station description calls the water tower built over an old Forest Service lookout tower. A Hoosier National Forest page, quoted by Indiana Fire Towers, says the Navy's Burns City depot operated four towers in World War II. The sources do not say which account is right, so the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Build date and origin of the water-tank tower are unknown; the sources conflict on whether it began as a Forest Service or a Navy tower. Cab removal rests on the FFLA Standing* footnote, not on a site photo we checked. Access and climbing status come from one Indiana Fire Towers visit report (February 2025). The brief's 'NSA Crane' name is the Register's title; the Register's location line reads Naval Weapons Station Crane.
